name: Animal Charity Evaluators (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Moves money: each animal charity it reaches, read live, brings its own countries.
summary: Animal Charity Evaluators evaluates animal advocacy charities, recommends the most effective, and passes donors' money to them through its Recommended Charity Fund and to small groups through its Movement Grants; this model covers all its own spending in its year to March 2025 ($1.72M; the $4.6M of grants it passed on are the recipients' cost). By its own surveys, with unrecorded gifts and our non-response step, it caused about $5.7M of giving to animal charities that year, three dollars per dollar it spends, valued at its Recommended Charities' figures on this site (ACE's own evaluations of them) weighted by its fund's split, shifted money only for its gain over an ordinary animal charity, and the next dollar at 30% of the past average: about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 at the site's animal weights. The result moves most with the animal weights and its next-dollar figure; no branch is discounted for missing data, since money moved is counted.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.explainer: Gifts to its Recommended Charity Fund, gifts to the charities directly because of its recommendations, and grantmakers' funding it influenced: at least $12.3M in its fiscal year, the year of the accounts above.

rows.label: Donations ACE recorded or traced, April 2024 – March 2025 (US$)
Share of donors' recorded giving ACE estimates it caused
rows.explainer: Its own estimates: $6.4M of the $12.3M to Recommended Charities 'would not have been received' without it, and $0.84M of the $1.2M of Movement Grants, from its surveys of donors who give to its Recommended Charities directly, of grantmakers and of past Recommended Charities and grantees. The $1.1M of grantmakers' funding it counts is taken out here and counted on its own (grantmakers_moved): 45% of the recorded giving. That is the shared own-effect question (normalization.md 2.8: the organisation's own survey), new money and money shifted from other charities together; whether it is new is the separate new-money share. Grantmakers' gross influenced funding isn't published, so it stays in the denominator: the share shown is slightly low; the dollars it caused are not.

rows.label: Unrecorded giving: ACE-influenced donations it has no data on, as a multiple of what it recorded
rows.explainer: Our judgment: ACE gives its figure as 'at least $12.3 million' and calls its cumulative total 'likely an underestimate' (its December 2024 announcement of the influenced-giving reports), since donors who give to a Recommended Charity without saying why aren't counted. 1.1 (1.0 to 1.3), applied to the direct gifts only (recorded giving less what came through its own funds, through_ace_donations): no published figure for what it misses; the low end takes its count as complete, the high end allows that direct gifts from donors who never say why are a large uncounted group.

rows.label: Share of the recorded giving whose donors or funders answered ACE's surveys
rows.explainer: Our judgment: ACE publishes no response rates. Its estimate traces gifts through its own fund (the $5.04M of supported-charity contributions, p. 4, about 37% of the giving recorded) and grantmakers it contacted, whose influence it asked about directly, and extrapolates the rest from surveys of donors who give directly. Anchored on the share of giving that answered in the other meta models' own surveys: Effektiv Spenden about a fifth of donors, GiveWell 42% of its surveyed donors' giving; 40% (20% to 70%).

rows.label: Survey-response step
rows.explainer: The shared rule for an organisation's own donor survey: those who didn't answer are less engaged, influenced at half the respondents' rate (a quarter to all). ACE's estimate makes no such adjustment that it publishes.

rows.label: Share of donors' recorded giving ACE caused (its own effect)
rows.explainer: ACE's own estimate with the shared non-response step: about 32%, beside the shared 30% for a meta charity without a survey and GiveWell's 59% from its own survey.

rows.label: Donors' money ACE moved that would not otherwise have reached the charities (US$)
rows.explainer: Recorded giving, with the unrecorded part of the direct gifts (giving through ACE's own funds is in its accounts), times its own effect: about {{row:donors_moved}}.

rows.label: Grantmakers' funding ACE's recommendations steered to its Recommended Charities (US$)
rows.explainer: $1.1M that grantmakers told ACE its recommendations influenced: they answered directly, so no survey-response step; valued below as shifted money only, since grantmakers fund animal work anyway (as the site's GiveWell model treats Open Philanthropy's money).

rows.label: Money ACE moved to animal charities that would not otherwise have reached them, April 2024 – March 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Donations to its Recommended Charities and Movement Grants net of what would have reached them anyway, and the grantmakers' funding it steered: about $5.7M, three dollars for each dollar of its own costs. ACE's own figure of $6.05 per dollar is for its evaluation spending only and before the non-response step.

rows.label: Average wait from a gift to ACE's funds to the grant (years)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: its Recommended Charity Fund pays out twice a year (August and February; $1,837,446 in February 2025, its fundraising post) and Movement Grants run in rounds, so a gift waits about a quarter of a year on average plus the time to pay out. Its year-end balance held for charities ($625,554 for Recommended Charities and $1.45M for Movement Grants, Note 8, p. 12) against the $5.04M received gives about 0.4 years, inflated by December's giving peak; 0.3 years (0.1 to 0.5).

Value of a dollar to the charities ACE moves money to (its own split, live), units of value
rows.explainer: Where the money ACE caused went in its fiscal year 2024–25 ($6.4M to its Recommended Charities, $0.84M as Movement Grants), by the site's rule for an organisation's own split (normalization.md 2.8). Its only per-charity split is its Recommended Charity Fund's two distributions of the year (July 2024 and February 2025, $2.36M; facts/meta.json ace_rcf_2024_25_*), which weight the eight Recommended Charities with a figure on the rankings, each read there under your values (The Humane League, Wild Animal Initiative, Shrimp Welfare Project, Sinergia Animal, Çiftlik Hayvanlarını Koruma Derneği, Dansk Vegetarisk Forening, Good Food Fund, Aquatic Life Institute); the giving it influenced directly is assumed to split the same way. Recipients without a model take the modelled average within the split and drop out: Faunalytics, Fish Welfare Initiative, Legal Impact for Chickens, New Roots Institute and The Good Food Institute among the Recommended Charities, and the Movement Grants' 32 small groups. Each figure on the rankings is ACE's own evaluation of that charity, the site's rule for any destination, not an independent check of ACE.

rows.label: Side effects of ACE's work beyond the money counted, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for an evaluator whose research is most of its work: {{row:moved_side_effects}} (−10% to +30%) of the modelled value. For ACE, positive: its charity reviews and research used by funders and donors who don't report it (other evaluators and funds that rely on its recommendations, beyond the $1.1M from grantmakers it counted), feedback that helps evaluated charities improve, and a field of small groups its Movement Grants keep alive; negative: the staff time evaluated charities spend on its reviews (it pays $24,000 towards it, p. 5), donors' attention drawn to what it can assess, and charities shaping their work to its criteria.

rows.label: Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium, Helen Keller Intl, New Incentives), each at GiveWell's figure for the charity on the rankings (its programmes and locations weighted by funding) under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: an ordinary charity of its cause, as 1× GiveDirectly is in global health), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the shared rule for an organisation that moves money within a cause other than global health (animal-welfare). Shifted money was going to be given anyway, to an ordinary charity of the same cause; it is credited only for the gain. An ordinary charity stands to its cause's charities on the rankings as GiveDirectly (GiveWell's model, times a shared multiple, 1×, from 0 to 3×) stands to global health's: GiveDirectly's live result over the global-health charities' (#cause:global-health), times the animal-welfare charities' (#cause:animal-welfare), all live under your values.

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone. The donors gave it, so the organisation is credited its share of that good (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of a dollar all shifted (given anyway, now to a better use), at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: Money that would have been given or spent anyway counts only for the gain over where it would have gone: a grantmaker's grants, or spending that research or advice changed. Its owners spent it, so the organisation is credited its share of that gain (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of the money ACE moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Donors' money moved (money through ACE after its wait) × the net value of a dollar moved, and the grantmakers' funding, all shifted, at the gain over an ordinary animal charity (moved_dollar_value − prior_dollar_value), with the side effects.

rows.label: Donors' share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.formula: cost_total / (cost_total + if($resource_shares, salary_sacrifice + donors_moved * new_money_share + inkind_advertising, 0))
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, ACE's cost shares the outcome with its staff's forgone pay, the donors' new money it moved (grantmakers' funding is all shifted) and Google's donated advertising (a co-funder's in-kind gift, Convention 2).

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give
rows.explainer: A further dollar for ACE's operations: its past average per dollar, credited by share of resources and scaled to the next dollar.
